groups.summary: Task status lives in runtime state (git common-dir) and never travels with git; the Done summary lives in the tracked task file. flowctl done writes both in one call. On the read side, validate compared the tracked spec status against runtime-preferred task status, so a fresh clone - where runtime is absent and every committed sidecar says todo - failed unconditionally: 582 structurally-false errors on this repo's own clone, and the work skill's Phase 5 validate verify step guaranteed-red for any spec closed elsewhere, violating the repo's own fn-181 doctrine (a task looking not-started in committed files is never grounds for a finding). On the write side, the documented loop commits BEFORE done, so the receipt lands in a tracked file after the commit with zero signal - the final task's summary never reaches another checkout - and three doc surfaces stated three different orderings (issues #346, #347).
groups.title: One command writes across the durability boundary and neither side is told

groups.summary: The epic/task mismatch downgrades to a warning when the task status came from the committed snapshot AND that snapshot carries no runtime progress markers. Discrimination is content-based via a new committed_status_is_authoritative helper - key-presence cannot work because RUNTIME_FIELDS keys exist in every modern tracked sidecar, so the legacy branch is taken on every runtime-absent read. A non-todo status, assignee, claim, evidence, or block reason in the committed file means a pre-state-dir repo where committed status IS authoritative: still an error. Runtime-sourced mismatches: still errors. Exit code stays gated on errors only. Fresh-clone probe: the 582-error class became warnings; the 23 residual errors are genuinely real (ancient tasks missing required headings).

changeWalkthrough.thesis: The tracked/runtime durability boundary becomes honest on both sides: validate downgrades the structurally-false fresh-clone status mismatch to a warning (content-discriminated so legacy repos and runtime-sourced mismatches stay errors), done/block report the tracked receipt file they write plus a one-line advisory when it is left dirty, and the loop ordering - commit, done, stage the receipt - is stated identically on all three documented surfaces (issues #346 + #347, one contract break).
